title: Pediatric Tonsillectomy
description: Separate infection-driven from sleep-driven indications, know who needs polysomnography, and run the perioperative plan: dexamethasone, no antibiotics, no codeine, and overnight monitoring for high-risk children.
objectives: Apply the recurrent throat infection thresholds for tonsillectomy
Know which children need polysomnography before tonsillectomy
Recommend tonsillectomy for documented obstructive sleep apnea and counsel on persistence
Give dexamethasone and safe analgesia, and avoid antibiotics and codeine
Admit high-risk children overnight and document post-tonsillectomy bleeding

references.citation: Mitchell RB, Archer SM, Ishman SL, et al. Clinical Practice Guideline: Tonsillectomy in Children (Update). Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2019;160(1_suppl):S1-S42.
Marcus CL, Moore RH, Rosen CL, et al. A randomized trial of adenotonsillectomy for childhood sleep apnea. N Engl J Med. 2013;368(25):2366-2376.

Paradise JL, Bluestone CD, Bachman RZ, et al. Efficacy of tonsillectomy for recurrent throat infection in severely affected children. Results of parallel randomized and nonrandomized clinical trials. N Engl J Med. 1984;310(11):674-683.

start.text: A 6-year-old boy snores loudly every night with pauses in breathing his parents have watched. His teachers report behavior problems. He has also had 4 sore throats this year.

infections.text: His parents ask whether the sore throats alone justify removing his tonsils. What do you say?

options.label: Yes: four episodes a year is enough
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019 (strong): recommend watchful waiting for recurrent throat infection with fewer than 7 episodes in the past year, 5 a year for 2 years, or 3 a year for 3 years. Tonsillectomy is an option above those thresholds, when each episode is documented with fever over 38.3 °C, cervical adenopathy, exudate, or a positive strep test.

options.label: No: four episodes is below the threshold, so watchful waiting for infections; his sleep symptoms are a separate indication
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019 (strong): watchful waiting for fewer than 7 documented episodes in 1 year, 5 a year for 2 years, or 3 a year for 3 years. In Paradise's trials of children above these thresholds, surgery reduced infections for 2 years, but many unoperated children had few, mild episodes. His snoring with apneas and behavior problems are the stronger reason to assess.

high_risk.text: His tonsils are large and nearly meet in the midline, and his BMI is above the 95th centile for his age. Before any surgery, what does he need?

options.label: Polysomnography
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: before tonsillectomy, refer children with obstructive sleep-disordered breathing for polysomnography if they are under 2 or have obesity, Down syndrome, craniofacial abnormalities, neuromuscular disorders, sickle cell disease, or mucopolysaccharidoses.

options.label: Proceed to adenotonsillectomy on history and examination
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: obesity is one of the conditions that require polysomnography before tonsillectomy in children with obstructive sleep-disordered breathing.

standard.text: He has none of the high-risk conditions, but his tonsils are small on examination, which does not fit the severity his parents describe. What next?

options.label: Polysomnography, because history and examination disagree
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: advocate for polysomnography before tonsillectomy in children without high-risk conditions when the need for surgery is uncertain or the examination and the reported severity of sleep-disordered breathing disagree.

options.label: Tonsillectomy based on the parents' description alone
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: when the examination and the reported severity disagree, advocate for polysomnography before deciding on tonsillectomy.

psg.text: Polysomnography shows obstructive sleep apnea: apnea-hypopnea index 12 events/hour, oxygen saturation nadir 78%. Recommendation?

options.label: Tonsillectomy, warning that sleep-disordered breathing may persist or recur
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: recommend tonsillectomy for obstructive sleep apnea documented by polysomnography, and counsel that it may persist or recur. In CHAT, early adenotonsillectomy normalized polysomnography in 79% vs 46% with watchful waiting and improved behavior, quality of life, and symptoms, though not attention and executive function scores.

options.label: Watchful waiting for 12 months, then repeat the sleep study
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: recommend tonsillectomy for children with obstructive sleep apnea documented by polysomnography. In CHAT, surgery improved symptoms, behavior, quality of life, and polysomnography compared with watchful waiting.

periop.text: Which belong in his perioperative plan?

options.label: A single intraoperative dose of IV dexamethasone
A 5-day course of amoxicillin after surgery
Acetaminophen with codeine for breakthrough pain

periop.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: give a single intraoperative dose of IV dexamethasone (strong), and recommend ibuprofen, acetaminophen, or both for pain (strong). Do not give perioperative antibiotics (strong), and never prescribe codeine or codeine-containing medication under age 12 (strong). Monitor overnight as an inpatient for children under 3 or with severe OSA, meaning an apnea-hypopnea index of 10 or more or a saturation nadir below 80%; he has both.

bleed.text: On day 6 his parents bring him back after he spat out bright red blood at home; he has now stopped bleeding. How should this be recorded?

options.label: As secondary post-tonsillectomy bleeding, contributing to the surgeon's annual bleeding rate
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: follow up after tonsillectomy and document bleeding within 24 hours (primary) and later than 24 hours (secondary). Surgeons should determine their primary and secondary bleeding rates at least annually.

options.label: No record needed, as the bleeding stopped on its own
options.feedback: AAO-HNS 2019: document the presence or absence of primary (within 24 hours) and secondary (after 24 hours) bleeding, and determine bleeding rates at least annually.

fail_indication.text: Guideline Deviation: Tonsillectomy decision off the indications.

fail_psg.text: Guideline Deviation: Surgery without a required sleep study.

fail_periop.text: Safety Risk: Perioperative plan with antibiotics, codeine, or no monitoring.

fail_audit.text: Guideline Deviation: Post-tonsillectomy bleeding not recorded.

success.text: Case Complete: Right indication, safe perioperative care, and bleeding audited.
